processing: Green tea made in the Murakami area, generally steamed in the Japanese way; since 2015 a shared company has handled crude-tea processing to raise quality.
harvest_season: Spring first flush is the prized picking, and one recent bottled tea is made wholly from it. Snow covers the bushes through the winter before it.
appearance_dry: Dark green needles, as is typical of steamed Japanese green tea.
appearance_liquor: Clear yellow-green, as is typical of steamed green tea.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf, as is typical of steamed tea.
taste_profile: Noted for sweetness and aroma, with little astringency and a mellow finish, which locals put down to the snowy winter.

brewing.notes: Typical settings for sencha. Slightly cooler water favours the sweetness this tea is known for.

vintage_note: Usual for Japanese green tea: sold as the current year's harvest and best drunk within about a year, with first-flush lots valued most. Labels usually name the seller or grade rather than a year.
description:
Murakami-cha comes from Murakami in northern Niigata, on the Sea of Japan coast, and it is usually described as the northern limit of commercial tea growing in Japan. That is the point of it: tea this far north, in serious snow, is a rarity.

Bushes sit under snow through the winter, and locals credit this for a leaf that holds its goodness until spring. Processing follows normal green tea practice, and since 2015 a joint company set up by three tea shops and a farm has handled the crude-tea stage to lift quality.

The tea is known for sweetness and aroma and for being mellow rather than sharp. Treat it gently with moderately cool water and short later steeps. Detailed tasting notes are few, so taste it against a Shizuoka sencha to judge for yourself.

Buy from a Murakami shop if you can, and ask for first flush of the current year. A bottled first-flush green tea from Murakami launched in 2026, so the name is reaching further than it used to.
history:
The usual account starts in 1620, when a Murakami townsman, Tokumitsuya Kakuzaemon, brought tea seed from Uji and began growing it, laying the base for the trade. Other origin stories exist, so this is the traditional version rather than a settled fact.

The modern chapter is about holding on: the 2015 founding of Murakami Seicha pooled the local shops and a farm to improve quality.
